look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the upright, narrow spore-bearing pair of basal pinnae that rises above the broad green sterile part of the frond. These are fertile fern leaf divisions, NOT flowers. Check the straw-colored stalk and once-pinnate blade with 4–7 pairs of mostly lanceolate pinnae.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Anemia mexicana as a species with two accepted varieties; Master Plant Pool source is species-level. Do not infer var. mexicana from an unvouchered source photo. Project follows Schizaeaceae as in its existing family lesson and POWO.

morphology_keys.habit: Terrestrial fern of lightly shaded limestone rock habitats; fronds arise along a creeping rhizome, rather than from a single tight crown.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Sterile green blade roughly triangular to lanceolate and once pinnate, typically 4–7 pairs of lanceolate pinnae with finely serrulate edges; straw-colored petiole.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Ferns have no flowers or seeds. Sporangia are concentrated on a distinctive erect pair of narrow fertile pinnae near the base of the blade; these can project above the sterile blade.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: No fruit or seed; examine mature sporangia and ridged spores on fertile pinnae.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Creeping rhizome with dark hairs; inspect the long straw-colored frond stalk.

confused_with: Anemia adiantifolia (much more finely divided sterile blade; primarily a different regional species)
Adiantum capillus-veneris (fan-shaped pinnules and marginal false indusia, not an erect fertile basal pair)
Asplenium resiliens (slender black rachis and linear sori on underside of ordinary pinnae)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Anemia mexicana carries the spore-producing parts on a specialized erect basal pinna pair. Maidenhair ferns bear sori under rolled leaflet edges; spleenworts have elongate sori on the underside of ordinary pinnae.
